Nowogrod Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nowogród, Poland

Not demolished. Nowogród's Jewish community, settled in the 19th century, numbered 514 people by 1921, most murdered during WWII. This cemetery certainly existed by 1836, when funeral income was recorded in the budget of the town's Synagogue Supervision. In September 1939, the Polish army used the cemetery's strategic hilltop location to defend the Narew River line, digging trenches still visible today; afterward, some residents used tombstones as grinding discs and building material, and the land was used for cattle grazing. In 2005, participants in a Lauder Foundation educational camp returned a recovered tombstone to the site, and in 2017 town authorities moved 18 more tombstones, extracted from a private building's foundations, back to the cemetery.
